# Installation, Environment & Runtime {#sec-install}

This chapter covers how PhyloTrace is installed and what it needs at runtime: the
two separate dependency worlds, the local files it keeps outside the database,
logging, and how it is launched. Installation instructions in full are in the
project `README.md`; this chapter explains the *shape* of the runtime so a
maintainer understands what is where and why.

## Two dependency worlds {#sec-install-deps}

PhyloTrace's dependencies split cleanly in two, and keeping them separate is a
deliberate architectural rule (@sec-arch-conda):

| World | Manifest | Holds | Managed with |
|---|---|---|---|
| **R packages** | `renv.lock` + `dependencies.R` | ~40 R libraries the Shiny app runs on | `renv` |
| **CLI tools** | `environment.yml` | pyMLST, AMRFinderPlus, abritamr, `blat`, `mafft` | Conda |

The Shiny app runs under **system R** with its `renv` library; the Conda
environment named `PhyloTrace` holds *only* the external command-line toolchain
the app shells out to. `renv` is activated automatically by `.Rprofile`, so
opening the project uses the locked library.

```{.yaml filename="environment.yml"}
# Rebuild from scratch:   conda env create -f environment.yml
# Update an existing env:  conda env update -f environment.yml --prune
```

::: {.callout-important title="Why pin the tools"}
`environment.yml` pins pyMLST to 2.2.2 (via pip, non-editable) and the AMR tools
to fixed versions, because the typing/parsing logic in `loop-pymlst.sh` and
`pymlst.R` is written against those exact outputs. An editable install from a
since-deleted checkout is what originally broke scheme downloads — hence the
non-editable pin. Treat the environment as part of the code contract, not a loose
set of "latest" tools.
:::

## System requirements {#sec-install-sys}

From the `README.md`, as guidance rather than hard limits:

| Component | Recommendation |
|---|---|
| OS | Any Linux distribution running R and Conda (Windows via WSL) |
| Browser | A current Chromium-family browser (Chrome, Brave, Chromium, …) |
| Storage | ≥ 250 GB — assemblies and databases add up |
| RAM | ≥ 8 GB |
| CPU | Multi-core, ≥ 2.5 GHz |

Typing whole-genome assemblies is the resource-hungry step; browsing and
visualizing an existing database is light.

## Local state outside the database {#sec-install-state}

Almost everything PhyloTrace remembers is *inside* the loaded `.db`
(@sec-arch-state). The exception is a small application-state directory,
resolved by `app/logic/paths.R`:

```{.r filename="app/logic/paths.R"}
#' Base directory path for local application data storage (`~/.local/share/phylotrace`).
app_local_share_path <- file.path(path_home(), ".local", "share", "phylotrace")
```

It holds `state.json` (the last-opened database, so the landing page can offer
"Last used: …") and the session logs. `stat_json` is read from it at startup and
rewritten by `main.R` on each database load (@sec-arch-nav).

## Logging {#sec-install-logging}

`app/logic/logging.R` is the central logging sink. `start_session_log()` opens a
fresh log per database load, its header naming the database so later lines need
not repeat it; `log_event()` writes structured, timestamped entries to both the
file and the console (`main.R` logs reloads and resets, @sec-arch-nav). The
Rhino-level log level is set in `config.yml` (`rhino_log_level`,
`rhino_log_file`).

## Launching the app {#sec-install-launch}

On Linux the installer registers a desktop launcher; the app also starts from a
terminal via the project's run script, which opens a browser tab pointed at the
local Shiny server. If the desktop launcher cannot find a browser, the
`R_BROWSER` environment variable selects one by executable name (see `README.md`
for the per-browser values). On Windows the app runs inside WSL by the same Linux
steps.

::: {.callout-important title="The app is local — what does and does not leave the machine"}
PhyloTrace is a *local* application: the server, the database and the toolchain
all run on your own computer, and the browser tab talks only to `localhost`.
Assemblies, isolates and metadata never leave the machine unless you explicitly
export or share a database file. The only outbound network calls are downloading
a scheme (@sec-tech-schemes), resolving a classical-MLST scheme (@sec-tech-typing), and
geocoding places for the map (@sec-tech-engines-map).
:::

## Chapter summary

- Dependencies split into `renv` (R packages, the app) and Conda (CLI tools);
  the app runs under system R, not the Conda env.
- The external toolchain is version-pinned as part of the code contract.
- Local state outside the database is a small `~/.local/share/phylotrace`
  directory (`state.json` + logs); everything else lives in the `.db`.
- Logging is centralized per session; launching opens a `localhost` browser tab,
  with `R_BROWSER` selecting the browser if needed.
